findings.finding: The front vertical adjustment is a compact upward-facing scalloped knob, exposed shaft and brass split collar in a cylindrical mount, with a separate bored cylindrical lower foot. The clearance1 tall graduated micrometer and raised rectangular bracket do not reproduce this construction.
findings.plan: Reconstruct the compact drive and genuine bored foot, preserving positive full-stroke clearance and the screw coupling.

findings.finding: Horizontal micrometers use split clamp blocks with actual transverse bores. The current mounting clamp is a solid box visually covering the collar.
findings.plan: Machine the visible bore and split without changing the sample-X grip position or its 1 mm table clearance.

findings.finding: Photo231 shows balls seated between the rotary top and the workholder, with separate threaded preload rods. The old model had a 6.8 mm gap below each ball and rods through the ball centers.
findings.plan: Balls now tangent to the unchanged top/support planes; separate rods and socket heads occupy the photographed surrounding plate. Heater/sample positions and service routes stay fixed.

findings.finding: Refreshing the hose audit exposed a previous route/handwheel interference at sample-X -12.5 mm and sample-Y +12.5 mm. Every offending surface was the unchanged sample-Y black handwheel.
findings.implemented: The fixed vacuum-routing knee is raised six mm; service endpoints and all instrument/robot target sites stay fixed. The route is a reconstructed safe service envelope, not a measured flexible-cable dynamics model.

changes: Replaced tall graduated Z micrometer/bracket with photographed shallow scalloped hand knob, exposed shaft, brass collar, cylindrical mount and genuinely bored lower thrust foot.
Drilled the four horizontal clamp bores and replaced their solid-box contact proxies with compound open-center supports.
Seated the three kinematic balls between the rotary top and heater support; separate preload rods and socket heads replace rods through floating ball centers.
Raised one vacuum-service routing knee by 6 mm to clear the sample-Y handwheel at the XY travel corner. Endpoints and instrument targets remain fixed.
limitations: Unmarked mount dimensions and 0.5 mm screw pitch remain photo-derived estimates.
The compact Z drive is an equivalent thrust-screw mechanism; concealed factory internals are not identified.
Service loops deform visually and are not flexible MuJoCo contact bodies.
The service pose grid is sampled, with stamp assembly at its rest/retracted configuration; it is not an all-pairs continuous configuration-space proof.
private_reference_policy: Raw laboratory photos and decoded video frames remain local; only rendered model previews are promoted.
